headline: Accepted $14,700 and $12,000 state safety grants and approved $8,000 from cable reserve for school equipment; Procopio agreement postponed.
summary: Residents spoke at length about council disputes, legal costs, and a lawsuit filed by the former Town Manager. Staff reported that fiscal year 2026 spending came in $193,764 under budget and previewed draft March 2027 warrant articles.
decisions: Accepted Bill Manning's resignation from the Recreation Commission, 4-0.
Accepted $14,700 from the NH Department of Safety for the 2027 Highway Safety Grant and authorized a grant agreement, 4-0.
Accepted $12,000 from the NH Department of Safety for the 2025 Homeland Security Grant and authorized a grant agreement, 4-0.
Approved an $8,000 withdrawal from the Cable Equipment Capital Reserve Fund to the Londonderry School District, 4-0.
Postponed the Off-Site Improvement Agreement for the Procopio project to November 2, 2026.
Postponed the Pavement Condition Index presentation to November 9, 2026.
Agreed by consensus to discuss a hiring policy at a future date.
Approved the October 5, 2026 meeting minutes, 3-0-1, with Vice Chair Faber abstaining.
By consensus, scheduled a Saturday FY2028 budget workshop for November 7, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

2. Discuss and authorize the Town Manager to execute the Off-Site Improvement Agreement for the Procopio project. Item postponed to November 2, 2026.

Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 1 
Londonderry Town Council Meeting Minutes 
Monday, October 19, 2026 | 7:00 p.m.  
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Londonderry Town Hall 
Council Members Present: 
Chair Ron Dunn 
Vice Chair Shawn Faber 
Councilor Dan Bouchard 
Councilor Deb Paul 
Council Members Absent: 
Councilor Ted Combes 
 
Meeting Video Link: 
http://173.166.17.35/internetchannel/show/14369?
channel=4 
Other Staff Present: 
Acting Town Manager Kim Alan Bernard 
Finance Director Justin Campo 
Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee 
Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis 
Minutes Prepared By: 
Kirsten Hildonen using Gemini Notebook AI 
 
A. CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Dunn called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance. 
B. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Brian MacDonald 
Address: 6 Picadilly Circle 
Represented Braver Angels (a national organization working to depolarize communities) and 
discussed scheduling a 'Managing Difficult Conversations with Colleagues' workshop for the 
Council. Reviewed potential meeting dates with the Council, concluding that November 23 or 
November 30, 2026, would be optimal as October 26 was too short notice and November 9 
conflicted with the Budget Committee. Chair Dunn agreed to poll Council members regarding 
available dates. 
Name: John Perez 
Address: 5 Wesley Drive 
Expressed deep disdain over Council dysfunction and municipal turmoil following recent 
executive decisions, announced that he was distributing signs, and reiterating his commitment to 
actively oppose the re-election of Council majority members. 
Name: Denise Drolet 
Address: 25 Kimbell Road 
Expressed strong frustration over the CCTV broadcast feed being disabled during the previous
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 2 
meeting recess, characterizing it as censorship. Criticized secret legal expenditures exceeding 
budget, hiring multiple outside law firms without transparent justification, and removing former 
Town Manager Shaun Mulholland without due process or the four-vote charter requirement 
under Section 3.02. 
Name: Sandra Lagueux 
Address: 2 Fiddlers Ridge Road 
Stated her concerns stem from the Council majority's actions, including driving up legal expenses, 
tabling policy modernizations, and altering Town Manager job qualifications. Asked for the 
immediate release of the final report from a prior anonymous investigation—which Vice Chair 
Faber stated would be released in early November following court proceedings—and criticized the 
lack of written specifics or a public hearing regarding the former Town Manager's removal. 
Name: Chris Oliverio 
Address: 1 Trolley Car Lane 
Commended Police Chief and Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard for exemplary municipal 
leadership, recommending that the Council model the job profile for the next permanent Town 
Manager after Chief Bernard. Shared personal experience with solar panel installations at his 
church in Derry, noting unexpected ongoing electrical costs ($40,000 annually) despite solar 
capacity. 
Name: Martha Smith 
Address: 38 Shasta Drive 
Asked who would be representing the Town in the lawsuit filed by the former Town Manager. 
Chair Dunn replied it would be Shaheen & Gordon. Councilor Bouchard asked why it wouldn’t be 
handled by Primex. Chair Dunn stated he would look into it. Ms. Smith is apprehensive about a 
firm without municipal experience handling the case. 
Name: Beth Marrocco 
Address: 4 Westwood Drive 
Questioned whether the Council had reflected on meeting rules and transparency, expressing 
concern over councilors collaborating outside public meetings. Urged the Council to follow 
established rules in the public light and expressed concern that council-driven legal expenses and 
liabilities would force town departments, including the library, to cut their budgets. 
Name: David Armstrong 
Address: 30 Sherwood Road 
Expressed disappointment with Council leadership for dividing the board into 3-2 and 4-0 factions 
rather than fostering five-member collaboration, questioned spending additional taxpayer funds 
on outside law firms, and criticized attempts to circumvent the Town Charter. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
Following public comment, Councilor Deb Paul addressed statements made at the October 5 
meeting regarding alleged complaints against herself and Councilor Bouchard, clarifying that 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard confirmed no active formal complaints exist. Councilor Paul 
summarized some of the legal matters and course cases that the Town is involved.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 3 
Councilor Dan Bouchard addressed the Council under Council rules, stating he would not be 
silenced regarding ongoing governance issues. He criticized Chair Dunn for allowing an 
unscheduled speaker to present for over seven minutes while strictly enforcing five-minute limits 
on others, criticized the lack of communication regarding lawsuits filed by the former Town 
Manager, questioned an unannounced $1,500 monthly stipend for the Acting Town Manager, and 
urged the Council to restore transparency and unity. 
C. BOARD APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS 
1. Resignation of Bill Manning from the Recreation Commission. 
The Council considered the resignation of Bill Manning from the Recreation Commission. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the resignation of Bill 
Manning from the Recreation Commission with regret and sincere appreciation for his service to the 
community. Seconded by Chair Dunn. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
D. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
1. Receive public input, discuss, and accept unanticipated revenue in the amount of 
$14,700.00 from the New Hampshire Department of Safety for the 2027 Highway 
Safety Grant, pursuant to RSA 31:95-b, III(a). 
Councilor Bouchard stepped out of the meeting at approximately 7:35 p.m. 
Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee presented Resolution 2026-19 regarding the FY2027 Highway 
Safety Grant from the NH Department of Safety, Office of Highway Safety, in the amount of 
$14,700.00. The grant provides pass-through funding for police officer overtime dedicated to 
speed enforcement, DUI patrols, distracted driving, seatbelt mobilization, and impaired driving 
control. 
Vice Chair Faber moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 3-0-0. 
Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Public Comment: 
Name: Ray Breslin 
Address: 3 Gary Drive 
Inquired what the grant is being used for. Controller Jardim-Lee confirmed it is strictly for 
overtime wages and is an annual pass-through grant awarded by the federal government through 
the State of New Hampshire. 
Councilor Bouchard returned to the meeting while Mr. Breslin was speaking. 
Councilor Bouchard moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-
0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the unanticipated 
revenue from the New Hampshire Department of Safety as presented in the amount of $14,700.00
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 4 
under RSA 31:95-b, III(a) and further authorizes the Town Manager to move forward in accepting this 
award and enter into a grant agreement with the New Hampshire Department of Safety. Seconded by 
Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
2. Receive public input, discuss, and accept unanticipated revenue in the amount of 
$12,000 from the New Hampshire Department of Safety through the 2025 Homeland 
Security Grant, pursuant to RSA 31:95-b, III(a). 
Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee presented Resolution 2026-20 regarding the 2025 Homeland 
Security Grant from the NH Department of Safety in the amount of $12,000.00. Funding supports 
local first responder overtime, specialized anti-terrorism training, exercises, and equipment for 
Londonderry Police Department operations at Manchester-Boston Regional Airport (MHT). 
Vice Chair Faber moved to open the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Bouchard. Motion carried 4-
0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Chair Dunn asked for public comment. There was none. 
Vice Chair Faber moved to close the public hearing. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0. 
Chair votes in the affirmative. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the unanticipated revenue 
from the New Hampshire Department of Safety as presented in the amount of $12,000.00 under RSA 
31:95-b, III(a) and further authorizes the Town Manager to move forward in accepting this award and 
enter into a grant agreement with the New Hampshire Department of Safety. Seconded by Councilor 
Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. Discuss and approve an expenditure from the Cable Equipment Capital Reserve Fund 
to the Londonderry School District in the amount of $8,000. 
Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee presented Order 2026-19 regarding the annual withdrawal from the 
Cable Equipment Capital Reserve Fund. Under the franchise agreement with Comcast, the town 
receives $32,500 annually for PEG access support, of which $8,000 is allocated to the 
Londonderry School District for educational television programming and studio equipment 
(including hard drives, microphones, and streaming headsets). 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approves the withdrawal request 
and directs the Town Treasurer to disburse $8,000.00 from the Cable Equipment Capital Reserve Fund 
to the Londonderry School District for educational programming equipment. Seconded by Councilor 
Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
2. Discuss and authorize the Town Manager to execute the Off-Site Improvement 
Agreement for the Procopio project. 
Item postponed to November 2, 2026.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 5 
3. Receive a presentation from the Department of Public Works regarding the 
Pavement Condition Index (PCI). 
Item postponed to November 9, 2026. 
4. Receive a presentation from the Department of Public Works and Weston & Sampson 
regarding Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) stormwater requirements. 
Deputy Director of Public Works James Danis and Jaurice Schwartz from Weston & Sampson 
delivered a detailed presentation on Londonderry's Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System 
(MS4) permit compliance and surface water quality requirements under EPA regulations. The 
presentation covered the six Minimum Control Measures (MCMs), ongoing catch basin cleaning 
and street sweeping programs, illicit discharge detection and elimination (IDDE) protocols, 
stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPP) for municipal facilities, and chloride reduction 
strategies. Discussion followed regarding catch basin cleaning equipment efficiency, maintenance 
costs, and budget tracking. 
5. Receive a fiscal update for Fiscal Year 2026 year-end results and the unaudited first 
quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. 
Finance Director Justin Campo presented the unaudited financial status for Fiscal Year 2026 
year-end and the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. For FY2026, total municipal expenditures and 
encumbrances totaled $45,076,231 against a budgeted appropriation of $45,269,995, ending the 
fiscal year $193,764 under budget (99.57% spent). For FY2027 Q1 (July 1 – September 30, 2026), 
departmental expenditures totaled $12,148,212 against a budgeted appropriation of 
$48,217,746 (25.19% spent, exactly tracking the 25.21% benchmark). In addition, ongoing water 
expansion projects received $1,500,000 in state grant funds and $1,565,806.79 from the state 
PFAS Remediation Loan Fund. 
6. Review the initial drafts of projected warrant articles for the 2027 Town Meeting. 
Finance Director Justin Campo and Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard presented a preliminary 
overview of draft warrant articles for the March 2027 Town Election (FY2028). Key draft articles 
include: Warrant Article #2 (Leach Library Renovation Bond for $1,418,117 with first-year debt 
service of $209,173); Warrant Article #5 (IAFF Local 3160 Collective Bargaining Agreement); 
Warrant Article #6 (Teamsters Local 633 Library CBA); Warrant Article #8 (Establishing a Town-
Wide Communication Systems and Equipment Expendable Trust Fund for $300,000 from 
Unassigned Fund Balance to eliminate radio dead zones); Expendable Maintenance Trust Fund 
($800,000); Roadway Maintenance Expendable Trust Fund ($650,000); Fire Department 
Equipment Capital Reserve ($600,000); Fire Truck Capital Reserve ($400,000); Information 
Technology Capital Reserve ($350,000); Establish and Fund a Revolving Fund for Fire Alarm 
Services; Leach Library Non-Capital Reserve ($20,000); Transportation Capital Reserve; and 
Water System Capital Reserve ($200,000). Key statutory deadlines noted: January 8, 2027 
(petition articles with bond), January 12, 2027 (standard petition articles), February 6, 2027 
(Deliberative Session), and March 9, 2027 (Election Day).
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 6 
Councilor Bouchard and Vice Chair Faber discussed whether the Public Works position should be 
in the budget or on a warrant article. Councilor Paul advocated that all of the positions should be 
treated the same and asked that the policy be put in place. The Council came to a consensus to 
discuss a policy around hiring at a future date. 
F. OLD BUSINESS 
None. 
G. APPROVAL OF CONSENT ITEMS 
1. Town Council Meeting Minutes from October 5, 2026 
Councilor Bouchard moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by Councilor 
Paul. Motion carried 3-0-1, with Councilor Bouchard, Councilor Paul, and Chair Dunn voting in favor, 
and Vice Chair Faber abstaining due to absence from the October 5 meeting. 
H. OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Liaison Reports 
Councilor Dan Bouchard raised questions regarding a Saturday gathering on Stokes Road 
involving Chair Dunn, Vice Chair Faber, the Fire Department, and local residents concerning the 
Stokes Road bridge. Councilor Bouchard expressed concern that the full Council was not notified 
in advance and asked whether funds were being transferred back from Hall Road to Stokes Road. 
Chair Dunn and Vice Chair Faber clarified that they attended as individual councilors to address 
constituent safety concerns and that a formal public hearing on the matter is scheduled for 
November 2, 2026. 
The Council discussed the schedule for the Fiscal Year 2028 initial budget presentations. By 
Council consensus, the Saturday budget workshop was scheduled for November 7, 2026, from 
10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. 
2. Town Manager Report 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard provided a brief operational update regarding ongoing 
municipal department coordination and FY2028 budget preparation. 
I. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Richard Bielinski 
Address: 89 Hall Road 
Expressed frustration over feeling disenfranchised by Council leadership, criticized lack of direct 
answers to resident inquiries, raised concerns regarding CCTV broadcast interruptions, and called 
for greater accountability and responsiveness to taxpayers.
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — October 19, 2026 
Page 7 
Name: Sandra Lagueux 
Address: 2 Fiddlers Ridge Road 
Clarified her earlier remarks regarding Town Manager job qualifications, quoting Acting Town 
Manager Kim Bernard ("What we allow is who we become") to urge transparency and criticize 
spending and charter non-compliance. Inquired about the historical email BCC practice, 
prompting Chief Bernard to confirm it was not in place during his prior interim tenure and Vice 
Chair Faber to clarify job description origins. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
J. NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
None held. 
K. ADJOURNMENT 
Vice Chair Faber moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 4-0-0. 
Chair votes in the affirmative. The meeting adjourned at 10:28 p.m. 
L. MEETING SCHEDULE 
• November 2, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 7:00 p.m. 
• November 7, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 10:00 a.m. (FY2028 Initial Budget 
Presentation) 
• November 9, 2026; Moose Hill Council Chambers; 6:00 p.m.
